catalog_quote: 6.1.2.5 Ο τονισμός Στα ΑΛ απαντούν λέξεις α) οξύτονες, π.χ. [pənóɲ] 'δουλεύω', [pərðé] 'χάμω', [kuʃurí] 'ξαδερφός', [ʃtəpí] 'σπίτι', [aɣaθó] 'αγαθός' κτλ. β) παροξύτονες, π.χ. [véte] 'πηγαίνω', [pərpára] 'μπροστά', [búrrə] 'άντρας', [nátə] 'νύχτα', [i gʎátə] 'πλατύς' κτλ. γ) προπαροξύτονες, π.χ. [ŋgróhemi] 'ζεσταινόμαστε', [príftəra] 'παπάδες', [étimo] 'έτοιμος', [çə́mərə] 'απέναντι' κτλ. δ) αντιπροπαροξύτονες, π.χ. [ŋgróhəɲənə] 'ζεσταίνουν', [príftəratə] 'οι παπάδες', [ə́ndərəsə] 'του ονείρου' κτλ. Λέξεις που να τονίζονται στην πέμπτη συλλαβή από το τέλος δεν υπάρχουν, συχνά όμως αναπτύσσεται στα πολυσύλλαβα αριθμητικά δευτερεύων τόνος, π.χ. [kátrəməðjétə] 'δεκατέσσερα', [pésəməðjétə] 'δεκαπέντε' κτλ. Ο τονισμός στα ΑΛ είναι συνήθως παραδειγματικός εκτός από λίγα αρχαϊκά ή δάνεια ονόματα, όπου παρατηρείται εναλλαγή ανάμεσα στον ενικό και τον πληθυντικό, π.χ. [ɲerí] – [ɲérəz] 'άνθρωπος – άνθρωποι' ... Το ίδιο, σε λίγα ρήματα παρατηρείται εναλλαγή στον τονισμό ανάμεσα στον ενεστώτα και τον αόριστο, π.χ. [fʎás] – [fóʎa] 'μιλάω – μίλησα' ... Αντίθετα, εναλλαγές στην θέση του τόνου χωρίς μορφολογική αξία συνηθίζονται στο κλιτικό παράδειγμα αντωνυμιών και σε ορισμένα άκλιτα ... [p. 238] Όλες οι παραπάνω περιπτώσεις είναι θεωρητικά ελεύθερες ποικιλίες. Ωστόσο στη μεγάλη πλειοψηφία των περιπτώσεων οι ομιλητές επιλέγουν τους παροξύτονους τύπους.

new_statements.translation: 6.1.2.5 Stress. In Laconian Arvanitika (ΑΛ) there occur words that are a) oxytone [final stress], e.g. [pənóɲ] 'I work', [ʃtəpí] 'house' […] b) paroxytone [penult], e.g. [véte] 'I go', [búrrə] 'man' […] c) proparoxytone [antepenult], e.g. [ŋgróhemi] 'we get warm', [príftəra] 'priests' […] d) stressed on the fourth syllable from the end, e.g. [ŋgróhəɲənə] 'they warm', [príftəratə] 'the priests' […]. Words stressed on the fifth syllable from the end do not exist, but a secondary stress often develops in polysyllabic numerals, e.g. [kátrəməðjétə] 'fourteen' […]. Stress in ΑΛ is usually paradigmatic [fixed throughout the paradigm], except for a few archaic or borrowed nouns, where an alternation between singular and plural is observed, e.g. [ɲerí] – [ɲérəz] 'man – men'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress position is lexically fixed and not predictable from word shape: words may be stressed on the final, penultimate, antepenultimate or fourth-from-last syllable (never the fifth). Within a paradigm the stress normally stays on the same syllable of the stem (columnar/'paradigmatic' stress), so inflection does not move it, apart from a handful of archaic or borrowed nouns (sg/pl) and a few verbs (present/aorist). Some pronouns and indeclinables show free variation between penultimate and final stress, with penultimate preferred.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Polysyllabic numerals (teens 11-19) often develop a secondary stress, e.g. [kátrəməðjétə] 'fourteen', [pésəməðjétə] 'fifteen' (p. 237; p. 261: 'on the first syllable'). No general statement of rhythmic secondary stress in other words.
new_statements.exceptions: Singular/plural stress alternation in a few archaic or borrowed nouns ([ɲerí]–[ɲérəz] 'man–men', [i máð]–[tə məðéɲ] 'big', [ðáskaʎ]–[ðaskáʎ] 'teacher', [mástor]–[mastórə]); present/aorist alternation in a few verbs ([fʎás]–[fóʎa] 'speak', [θər(r)és]–[θírra] 'call'); free variation without morphological value in clitic-paradigm pronouns and some indeclinables ([kío]~[kió], [kə́ta]~[kətá], [kə́tu]~[kətú], [sívjet]~[sivjét], [síkur]~[sikúr]); emphatic retraction in [éde]~[edé] 'and'; doublets [proscéfaʎ]~[proscefáʎ] mirroring Greek προσκέφαλο/προσκεφάλι; [zúbəro]~[zubəró], [ʃúto]~[ʃutó], [ʎə́m]~[ʎəmó] where the oxytone form looks newer. Also p. 232: the first element of the diphthongs /ié/, /uá/ can never bear stress in ΑΛ, unlike Albanian and the other Arvanitika dialects.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in citation/inflected forms of Laconian Arvanitika (ΑΛ = αρβανίτικα Λακωνίας, the Arvanitika villages of the SE Peloponnese south of Tsakonia), described from the author's own fieldwork and compared with Attic-Boeotian Arvanitika (ΑΑΒ) and Standard Albanian. Stress is marked on every transcribed form; free variants in pronouns/adverbs are noted as theoretically free but paroxytone forms are chosen in the great majority of cases (p. 238). Greek loan verbs are adapted with stress moved to the final syllable (p. 274).
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes Laconian Arvanitika (ΑΛ = αρβανίτικα Λακωνίας: the Arvanitika villages of the south-eastern Peloponnese south of Tsakonia, Liosis 2007: 75), one local dialect of arva1236; Glottolog lists no dialect subdivisions for arva1236, so no separate glottocode. Liosis notes at least one accent difference from the Attic-Boeotian dialect (ΑΑΒ, described by Sasse 1991) and Standard Albanian: in ΑΛ the first element of the diphthongs /ié/, /uá/ never carries stress (ΑΛ /dié/ vs ΑΑΒ /díe/, ΑΛ /kruá/ vs ΑΑΒ /krúa/), with Argolid Arvanitika (ΑΑ) intermediate ([grúa] ~ [gruá]) (pp. 232-233). Reinhold 1855 covers the Poros/Hydra/Spetses variety.

sources.note: Laconian Arvanitika has oxytone, paroxytone, proparoxytone and pre-antepenult-stressed words (never 5th from end); stress is 'usually paradigmatic' (fixed through the paradigm) except sg/pl alternation in a few archaic/loan nouns and pres/aor alternation in a few verbs; secondary stress in polysyllabic numerals; free stress variation in clitic pronouns and some indeclinables, paroxytone forms preferred (p. 238); first element of /ié/, /uá/ never stressed in this variety unlike Albanian/other Arvanitika (p. 232, citing Sasse 1991: 81).
No statement about stress or accent anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent: only a remark that phonology was influenced by Greek).
